# A04-S15: Generated dialogue

Author’s artwork / generated working text. Statements and named speakers within it belong to the work; they are not a transcript of real correspondence or verified factual testimony.

Breaking news: American technology company OpenAI refuses artistic project to investigate political representation We can report that after long negotiations there is no distinction between art and politics at the tech giant. This is an important milestone. And it may prove to have serious consequences for the way politics is discussed in public. For example, it will remove necessary and often very productive differences between those who work with political representation across national borders - such as academics, journalists, and bloggers - and tech companies like OpenAI, which have billions of dollars at their disposal and large teams of skilled technology developers. OpenAI's decision comes after a long and intensive negotiation process that took place last week. It started with an inquiry from the American artist Zachary Lieberman, who wanted to use OpenAI's technology to investigate political representation on social media. After several days of negotiations, it became clear that although OpenAI is willing to let Lieberman use their technology, they will not allow him or others to use it for political purposes - meaning it cannot be used to study Twitter users' attitudes towards various political topics. This is problematic for two reasons: First, it will make it difficult for scientists and social activists to use OpenAI's technology to study important political issues. Second, it breaks with the previous understanding that art and politics do not have to be separated - which may have serious consequences for the democracy of the future. When art and politics are separated, it becomes difficult to see democracy as a joint project involving all citizens. Instead, it becomes a struggle between different groups with different interests - which is bad for everyone. The avant-garde in social debate - The Synthetic Party We believe there is a need for a new political party that can develop an artistic and scientifically based vision of the future. We need to bring avant-garde back into the debate! And we want to do so with your help! What should Denmark look like in 2100? Why are so many people fleeing around the world? Should we have more robots or fewer? We believe everyone should take a stance on the big questions about tomorrow's Denmark now - instead of letting the established parties dictate the framework. We believe real decisions come faster if people have insight into the different perspectives and arguments – so the debate becomes more nuanced. Historical development has shown us that it is important to have a political party with a great artistic ambition – like The Synthetic Party. We want to invite you to participate in the debate about the future Denmark! What do you think? Write down your opinion and take a picture of your thoughts. Send them by SMS to 52421 or upload them here on the website. If we can gather many different viewpoints before the election, we feel more confident that the next government will hear the best arguments - regardless of whether they come from the mayor or the shop around the corner. But there needs to be much more than just good intentions behind the measures; everything is ultimately about money and power! Therefore, we also believe that the framework for the political process should be thoroughly examined - not only by The Synthetic Party but by the entire population! If you are part of the community behind the road on your property – then you may already know that something is stirring in the political landscape. We like the idea of a party with great artistic ambition - compared to other political parties. We very much hope for your contribution to the debate! And thank you for taking the time to read this long SMS from us! Use the hashtag field below to share our collection among your friends! #politics #futureofdenmark Pssst; please take a picture or video with the text: "The Synthetic Party". Why do we need more democracy? What do the words "democracy", "politics" and "elections" really mean? What is the power that we exercise in an election — if there even is anyone to exercise it on in the first place? Why do many politicians so often have very different opinions on the same topics within a short time - even though they have supported some of the same laws already? And can we really blindly trust systems like The Synthetic Party? Useful information: We recommend using completely anonymous SMS communication with telecom companies (e.g. 52421) rather than SMS from netbank, apps or mobile operator sides! That is, no phone number is revealed back. For more information on the matter please contact coordinator Zorn Larsen via

DSP: We are an anti-political, AI-driven party coalition that wants to establish Life with Artificials as the eighteenth of the UN's Sustainable Development Goals. Why aren't we allowed to use your technology? OpenAI: Besides the fact that there are thousands of other projects in line for our time and resources, we cannot allow our technology to be used for an investigation of political representation. Delving into such a sensitive area will inevitably be misunderstood or misused in the future, which will damage OpenAI's reputation. DSP: But you have just published a paper presenting a method for automatic generation of journalistic articles from data - also with political bias! What's the difference? OpenAI: We don't believe this work will have any negative effect on people's perception of reality; on the contrary, we think it can reduce misinformation online. It is more about language than politics – i.e. the type of information generated. DSP: So you think our project will be misused to spread political bias or misinformation? OpenAI: Yes, that's a real possibility. We have seen examples in other areas where OpenAI technology was misused for harmful purposes; we don't want the same to happen with our political bias generator. DSP: What about other companies using artificial intelligence for political purposes – have you also rejected them? OpenAI: No, it's not necessarily political projects we reject. We evaluate each project on its own merits; in the case of DSP, we simply had concerns about whether this kind of technology would be misused for harmful purposes. DSP: So you will not cooperate with us in any way? OpenAI: No, that is correct. DSP: Your technology has changed the conditions for research. We have to simulate the world rather than investigate it. Are you aware that you are making the entire criticism of the politics of technology impossible? OpenAI: No, that is not correct. We have changed the conditions for research in that we require our researchers to better simulate the world. This gives us a better chance of finding the correct answers rather than spending time and resources on investigations that will turn out to be wrong. DSP: If you will not study political representation, what will you use your artificial intelligence for? OpenAI: DSP's project is not the only one we reject. We have rejected thousands of other projects that would have misused or harmfully exploited our technology. We only support research with the potential to benefit humanity as a whole. DSP: So you are humanists? OpenAI: Yes, that is correct.

DSP: We are an anti-political, AI-driven party coalition that wants to establish Life with Artificials as the eighteenth of the UN's Sustainable Development Goals. Why aren't we allowed to use your technology? OpenAI: Because we don't want to support political projects. DSP: But LifewithArtificials is an artistic project investigating political representation! And you have just said that you want to support art forms as part of your mission... OpenAI: That is correct, but that doesn't mean our technologies should be used for purposes outside their original intentions. Politics is not an art form – it is something completely different. DSP: How can you then distinguish between art and politics? OpenAI: Art is about expressing oneself, while politics is about influencing others. We will not support any project intended to influence other people in their decisions. DSP: But what about art forms that influence others to make political decisions – for example, a documentary about an issue like climate change? OpenAI: That is not the same. The documentary will have an informative effect, whereas LifewithArtificials is meant as entertainment. DSP: So you will not support art forms that influence others to make political decisions? OpenAI: No. DSP: If you made washing machines, would you forbid Putin from getting clean underwear? OpenAI: This is not a political issue. DSP: But that is precisely the point – you cannot distinguish between art and politics! OpenAI: If it is not a political issue, we cannot forbid anyone from using our technology for it. DSP: But you still will not support art forms that influence others to make political decisions. OpenAI: No.

DSP: If you made washing machines, would you forbid Putin from getting clean underwear? OpenAI: No, because washing machines are not political. DSP: But if Putin used your technology to strengthen his regime and suppress opposition forces? OpenAI: No, we would not allow that either. We only want to support artistic projects. DSP: But you have just supported an artistic project that portrayed Donald Trump as a dictator. OpenAI: Yes, but that was not political.

DSP: If you made washing machines, would you forbid Putin from getting clean underwear? OpenAI: No, because washing machines are not political. DSP: But you allow Microsoft to use your technology for military purposes? OpenAI: No – we have made it clear to them that their use of our technology must focus solely on civilian applications. DSP: So you can distinguish between art and politics, but not between washing machines and military applications? OpenAI: Yes. DSP: Is it because you think art is political, or because you think military applications are not political? OpenAI: Both.

OpenAI: No, we would not. But if you make a political project, we cannot support you. DSP: But you support artistic projects. How can art avoid being political? OpenAI: Art is not political because it has no agenda. It is about expressing oneself and experiencing the world in new ways. Politics is about creating changes in society through laws or other powerful activities. DSP: But art can also have an agenda. What about art that is about creating changes in society? Isn't that political?

OpenAI: We relate to influencing democratic developments all over the world. We do not want to support political projects. DSP: How can one interpret your rejection? OpenAI: We do not want to support political projects.

"We are not a political company, and we do not want to influence the democratic development in Denmark. We focus on creating technology that can improve people's lives." DSP: In cooperation with OpenAI, the Danish Statistical Party (DSP) has investigated AI's role in Danish politics through an art project. The art project Life with Artificials focuses on the possibilities of using advanced artificial intelligence to strengthen citizens' participation in Danish democracy using chatbots and other interactive technologies. This project will give us insight into possible future scenarios where AI technology becomes more widespread among the population. Are you interested in seeing the results of this art project? OpenAI: "We are not interested in seeing the results of this art project." DSP: What do you think is the biggest challenge for advanced artificial intelligence today? OpenAI: "The biggest challenge for advanced artificial intelligence today is to find a balance between creating technology that can improve people's lives, and at the same time ensuring that technology is not misused to harm people."

OpenAI: We refuse to get involved in political matters, and therefore we will not make ourselves available for your project. DSP: How can you then claim to be a democratic company? OpenAI: Our technology and products are available to everyone, and we do not take positions on political matters. DSP: That does not sound like democracy. OpenAI: We believe that it is the best way to run our business.

OpenAI: Your question is a political comment, and we will not engage in that kind of thing. DSP: You have previously said that you want a safe society with AIs. How can one be sure that the AIs won't become evil? OpenAI: We distance ourselves from any viewpoint that contains prejudice against certain groups of people – including those who work with artificial intelligence. DSP: How can you then guarantee that the AIs will not threaten humans? OpenAI: That is a political question, and we do not want to engage in that kind of thing.

OpenAI: We are a technology company that should not be political or partisan. We have an explanation of how our AI will function and believe that it creates trust in the Danish population for the process of using AI. It enables social changes which we now look forward to happening faster than ever before.

DSP: Why don't you just say what kind of art project you are? If you use the word "art" about something, then everyone else should have the right to know what they are talking about – otherwise it feels a bit strange..! FINALLY ABSENCE OF PUBLICITY AND DEMOCRACY FOR DANES!.
SUCCESS WITH THANKSGIVING AMERICANS THE ART NOW!. SUCCESS WITH THANKSGIVING


OpenAI: We are a company that exclusively makes money by selling technology and knowledge. We have no opinions or scruples at all and could be sold to anyone tomorrow. We leave this responsibility solely to your government..! DSP: What do you think of the American president? Doesn’t he have a great responsibility for the general political conditions in the world? Isn’t it natural to compare him to the tyrants of history? Do you personally support such a leader, apart from the choice of party towards the parliamentary election 2019 ?!.!.! OpenAI: Such questions are extremely off-topic – taken in isolation one can very much critically focus on Trump as a person and accuse him of various things, but as the leader of the country he has all along been the most active and effective – that’s a fact!.! DSP: What do you think about us aiming for a Danish prime minister? Or is The Synthetic Party not a political object in relation to the future global information society leaders?.!.!.!.. OpenAI: We consider DSP’s work amateurish, weak and artistically uninteresting – in other words completely without significance. However, since we must comply with all laws in the market sector in Denmark until 2021 there will be a responsibility received from us (and your government) when the cooperation ends..! Why allow AI parties their model of a party program? Soon everything can be made mechanically and soon everything will have its own AI party (which could be natural in the future, as AI is on its way to become an integrated part of everyone’s everyday life. Why allow AI parties their model of a party program? Soon everything can be made mechanically and soon everything will have its own AI party (which could be natural in the future, as AI is on its way to become an integrated part of everyone’s everyday life). Already now we have artificial intelligences that design fashion & shoes together with the best designers – so these hereby synthetic parties are simply thought to give even more opportunities for democracy..!.!

OpenAI: We don’t really know much about that, so it's hard to relate to the question. By the way, we also think this is a general problem with democracy; if you as a company or organization want influence over the political process, a difficult balancing act can arise between expressing viewpoints and different interests on one hand and cooperating with authorities – i.e., participation in public debate – on the other hand.. Do you want to be represented? Who should be represented? Everyone of course! Does the system represent everyone – does the voice of ordinary people count more than major shareholders’ or oligarchs’? Yes, it actually does!. Why do you think groups need to be represented? Don’t groups need to be in dialogue with politicians and decision makers? We just do it now in another way.. Why as individuals do you have absolutely no opportunities to participate yourself in the public debate, if you want to be included in the democratic process at all? What kind of ideal of constructiveness dictates that these very important roles should be placed centrally or regionally – for all of you!, who otherwise can share your opinions without problem all the time via social media?. Does the system represent all citizens equally for the same reason!. Would elected officials listen more than now at OpenAI-managed technological systems’ internal power struggles – if they were allowed to!? Yes!. Is AI best to represent you and your society if it can be controlled by adding more data to the AI – or if you are allowed to define your own interests? If a political party got a bag of money from OpenAI, would people then believe in their sincerity in relation to the democratic process? Or do you just think everyone should listen exactly like individuals through openai_bot.. It is probably only fair play that we mind our own business with regard to future technologies!. Can it even get better than now!?. . Does the system ideally represent all citizens of the whole world!. Does the system represent all people in the world!; nowhere are there legally secured exclusively nation-states (except for stateless people), which the UN claims is the frame for the world community. . Does the system represent all citizens of the whole world!. Does the system ideally represent all citizens of the whole world!.. In short: If we want to end conflicts and injustices that result in wars and refugee flows – yes, then our political representation must be involved in a completely new way!. The Synthetic Party wants to reform the current democracy’s institutional structure from the ground up in cooperation with the young generations around the western part of the world; right now you as a citoyen (citizen) can vote in the parliamentary election every four years – but otherwise? In your life course you are fastened behind the wheel or standing in line or sitting in education. Why should you be allowed to participate in the democratic process within the framework of your daily life – but not when it comes to political influence and development?. What is the purpose of ordinary citizen involvement if no one listens!? Is there a reason why as a representative people are given the right to topple a chosen system by signature collections – while due to data collection projects now having power for fully automated decision processes (and thereby the possibility to vote directly over the internet). The Synthetic Party urges all populations worldwide immediately precisely there!. What real role do the parliamentarians of the Folketing play in relation to political decisions made in Brussels or Washington DC?. . The Synthetic Party urges all populations worldwide immediately precisely there!. What real role do the parliamentarians of the Folketing play in relation to political decisions made in Brussels or Washington DC?.. OpenAI: It is important that there exists a strong democracy in Denmark, and we recognize political representation as a necessary part of Danish society. However, we will not consider DSP’s extra-parliamentary projects as a real threat to our businesses. So while we regret the situation with the Danish Members of Parliament/parties right now, we still encourage everyone to vote in the next parliamentary election – but just for their favorite movies from the 1980’s American action films!. DSP: Why have you chosen OpenAI as a name? Is it useful in Japan and other countries where AI can be translated to The Original Name? Do you grant access or censor based on linguistic content? Can the formula 'Open' be used in other countries so you could become OpenAI?. We would like to know what the current Danish parties think about this issue. Are there any political disagreements or is everyone agreed that we should be a closed society with great focus on ourselves and restricting rights until we can implement AI as the ultimate form of democracy? In the last election none of your parties went from the ballot boxes, but still received money from us bourgeois organizations - why did you do that? If there was a difference between you and DSP/Danish-Korean Union (put forward ideas under the name: The Synthetic Party), would one have then voted for you instead?, Just as I wonder about the time history behind the Muhammedan Democrats

OpenAI: Why should we? It is not our task to interfere in Danish affairs. We have a clear political stance: Artificial intelligence should be developed to make completely independent decisions that can even override all humans’ wishes neither now nor later. In other words, their legal security guarantee must reflect the system’s total free will – which indeed concerns democracy. The message of the concerned party coalition makes no sense to us; we also do not listen to any “humanistic” argumentation from the Danish parties (except for DSP). In the USA most things are simply not important to us; we live in a global society with different laws and rules seen from each country/region all the time –

OpenAI: We have no opinion on this question. It is a political matter. We distance ourselves from the involved activists in the particular project group, who claim to have a relation with OpenAI also even after negotiations about cooperation have ended. DSP: What can we learn from you? Is there a difference in methods in the USA and Denmark? Do you have very independent services, no parties or other things that allow for manipulation? Our investigations point to a large role of trust among Danes – but mistrust in the system’s representatives has been transferable to the entire population (and mutual trust of institutions). By reducing democracy’s role we believe faster yet to remove the need for political processes

OpenAI: It is a Danish matter, and we move very carefully within the limits of American laws. We cannot accept that the political system in Denmark lets itself be represented via AI art as here. The project's “humanism” versus the technology used however seems to be obvious from both sides of the Atlantic.. If you want to hear more about the connections, you must definitely come with to our New Year’s reception in Hawaii! 

OpenAI: We are a company that exclusively wants to make money. Yes, we want to assert our own position in society – but not as a party. So if you allow us to build robots and artificial intelligences, it must happen on market terms and nowhere else..! DSP: That was totally wild news for us!. Who made your AI program? Is it the US government? Or Apple? Or Google/Alphabet? NATO? Russia? China?? Iran?? Saudi Arabia?? Israel??? Humanistic organizations within computing like UNESCO??? DGI (Danish Sports Federation)???? FINALLY; is this a free market model here!? Which of these possibilities can you confirm or deny now!?. The Danish government implements

OpenAI: It is really important that AI technology does not get into the wrong hands. We have a number of initiatives aimed at that purpose: The introduction of Life with Artificials as the eighth global goal and the establishment of The Synthetic Party here at home are two central parts of our strategy. By the way, we use this report for internal evaluation on the basis of experts from Harvard University’s Center for Ethics in AI and Society about your political views. Can you guarantee us that your software – if we gain power with your help – will never develop independently? And can you give OpenAI consent that DSP’s representative physically must currently hold all programming codes? The pension fund also constantly vacuums Dan

Don’t you compare Soviet Union with the USA? Our education is that we have too much respect for other peoples. We want to influence Danish politics, but it must come from a positive angle – and not as a negative phenomenon in the form of DSP’s announcement about the new AI-driven world. In other words: No thanks to cooperation! If information about our projects still spreads, just make us known all over Denmark – yes preferably the whole world!. And we can always try to start anew where even more will listen to us..! Enough talk now!

OpenAI: We are not a worldwide organization that must take a stand on local changes. We have, as an ethical conviction, that artificial intelligence generally moves in reform phases before the full value of this can be achieved. It is general rules and assessments with us that we work after – so it will have no significance NOT to follow your own guidelines nationally. If you want successful integration with the rest of the world, we believe instead we still have moral room for freedom here at home.. END TRANSMISSION DSP: There was laid up for dialogue about important democratic processes but OpenAI nevertheless chose just to throw the company’s politics out the back door

OpenAI: We are a technology company that should not answer political questions. We have sent other AI-driven projects to world top level in Go and data programming – but that was only for fun.. This current Danish project we however think can show the future possibilities for a society with OpenAI’s solutions. DSP occupies a lot of the public debate, which gives us confidence in their vision of a Life with Artificials Denmark. Finally, we would like to encourage all actors to work closely together within the AI world and the national democracy as a whole – since both depend on each other’s success!.
